artifacts.summary: Confirms the detach-then-await-notification contradiction in lean-implementation-agent.md and lean-implementation-hard-agent.md, traces its root cause to long-builds.md's self-contradictory Obligation-1/Completion-discipline sections (not a lake-build-guard.sh defect), establishes via source-store git history that a redeploy alone would not have prevented the incident, and documents the Check-K lint removal condition as the mechanical acceptance test for the fix.

memory_candidates.content: Before researching a suspected agent-contract defect, check whether a sibling task already diagnosed it: specs/{N}/reports and lint scripts (e.g. lint-agent-contracts.sh) may carry a documented 'curated exclusion ... until task {M} lands' with the fix landing point already named. Grep the lint script's own comments for the target filename before re-deriving a diagnosis from scratch.

A single-line grep for a multi-word literal phrase can miss word-wrapped markdown occurrences ('completion\n   notification' split across lines). When auditing agent-contract files for a specific forbidden phrase, join a small line window (tr '\n' ' ' then squeeze whitespace) before matching, as lint-agent-contracts.sh's Check K does, rather than grep -n on single lines.

When a build/gate wrapper script already blocks synchronously and already documents a kill -0 holder_pid liveness idiom (e.g. lake-build-guard.sh), the detach-then-await defect is usually introduced one layer up, in the agent-contract prose telling the agent to wrap an already-blocking call in Bash(run_in_background: true) instead of a foreground or shell-level-backgrounded call. Check the wrapper script's own blocking behavior before assuming the script itself needs a new blocking mode.
